title: GOD SENT ME AHEAD OF YOU

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'And now, do not be distressed and do not be angry with yourselves for selling me here, because it was to save lives that God sent me ahead of you.'" — Gen 45:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the great verses of the Old Testament, and we must be careful to hear it correctly.

Joseph does not say what they did was fine. He does not excuse the pit, the silver, or the lie. What he says is that God was working underneath their evil, and God's purpose was not defeated by it. "You sold me here" is true. "God sent me" is also true. Both, at the same time.

That is a mystery we cannot fully unravel, and Scripture does not ask us to. It simply holds the two together. Human beings are genuinely responsible for their sin, and God is genuinely sovereign over the outcome. Joseph will say it even more directly in chapter 50: you intended to harm me, but God intended it for good.

The same two truths meet at the cross. Wicked men crucified Jesus and were fully guilty of it — and yet Peter preached that it happened by God's deliberate plan and foreknowledge (Acts 2:23). The worst thing humans ever did became the means of the world's salvation.

This does not make your suffering good. It means your suffering is not wasted, and it is not outside God's reach.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you name a hard thing in your past that God has since used for good?
2. How do you hold together human responsibility and God's sovereignty without excusing sin?
3. What situation do you need to trust God with today, even without understanding it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not always understand how You work good out of terrible things. Help me trust that nothing in my life is outside Your reach, and that Your purposes cannot be defeated by anyone's sin. Amen.
